correctness.rationale: Exact rational stage elimination yields r_x(z) and its monotonic derivative; the two-state stationary projector gives M=Pi+r(I-Pi), reducing stochasticity to r >= -m/(1-m). Solving the complete threshold quadratic gives all probability branches, and analytic limits prove m=1/3, the square-root onset, and deterministic product positivity despite almost-sure recurrent negative one-step entries. A standalone Python 3 rational checker passed 4703 auxiliary checks; the infinite statements rely on the proof.

value.rationale: In finite-state kinetics, stochasticity of the entire numerical transition operator—not just scalar contractivity—is a natural physical invariant. The exact parameter-averaged probability, sharp one-third stationary balance frontier and square-root onset answer a concrete step reliability question for a recent random integrator. The dichotomy of infinitely many invalid local factors versus deterministically eventually positive cumulative propagators gives a meaningful new boundary for interpreting long-time computations.
